title: Beatrix and the Letter
premise: Felix Galloway, a courier for the collapsing Republic of Vessany, has survived nine years by carrying sealed orders and asking nothing. When an infant is abandoned at her safehouse with a note reading 'forget the face,' she recognizes the handwriting as that of the minister whose dispatches she carries—and realizes the child is evidence of a treasonous pact being sold to the republic's enemies. To save the girl and expose the betrayal, Felix must run the last open road through three checkpoints with the proof sewn into the child's swaddling, pursued by the very officers she once served. She reaches the border assembly at terrible cost, trading her own anonymity—her only protection—for testimony, and ends the book not as an invisible courier but as a named witness, raising the child in a republic reborn from the truth she carried.
about_author: T. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states. They write historical fiction about the small, expendable people who carry history in their hands.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Opening on the eve of the republic's fall: Felix memorizes and burns a dispatch, establishing her rules—invisible, unattached, unasked. Emotional beat: the cold comfort of a life measured in what fits in a satchel.

chapters.title: The Weight at the Door
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A crying bundle appears at her safehouse door with a note in Minister Corvane's hand: 'forget the face.' Inside the swaddling, a folded cipher sheet. Emotional beat: fear curdling into reluctant tenderness as the child grips her finger.

chapters.title: Nine Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Felix's POV. How she became a courier after her family's arrest, and why invisibility kept her alive. Emotional beat: grief revealed as the engine of her discipline.

chapters.title: The Hand I Know
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She deciphers enough of the swaddling document to see troop movements sold to the Karstine envoy—a pact signed by Corvane himself. Emotional beat: loyalty to the ministry cracking against the truth in her hands.

chapters.title: Orders Come Anyway
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A summons arrives: deliver one final dispatch through three checkpoints before the armistice seals the roads. The route passes directly toward the enemy lines. Emotional beat: dread—the trap and the escape route are the same road.

chapters.title: The Wet Nurse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. A displaced wet nurse agrees to travel with Felix and the child for passage money, hiding her own deserting brother's name. Emotional beat: two women negotiating trust with nothing but need as collateral.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: Ashford Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A courteous captain searches the coach while Felix performs the dull courier he expects; the cipher survives inside a feeding cloth. Emotional beat: terror masked as boredom, and the first taste of getting away with it.

chapters.title: The Face She Was Told to Forget
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At a waystation she finds a portrait miniature tucked in the swaddling—the child resembles Corvane's dead daughter. Emotional beat: the 'forget the face' order reframes as a father's desperate, cowardly love.

chapters.title: Marta's Brother
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Her brother surfaces among deserters sheltering them overnight; he recognizes Felix's courier seal and nearly betrays her position to buy his own amnesty. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by survival, foreshadowing Felix's own choice.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A checkpoint where travelers must declare their business aloud; Marta improvises a cover story so convincing it hurts. Emotional beat: the strange power of a lie told well, and guilt at how easily Marta lies for her.

chapters.title: Corvane's Shadow
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV, single interlude. The minister learns a courier left the capital with more than his dispatch and sends Captain Ilves to retrieve 'the package' quietly. Emotional beat: a powerful man discovering that mercy leaves fingerprints.

chapters.title: The Road Splits
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ilves catches up at a river ford; Felix must choose between the fast military road and the flooded marsh path with an infant. Emotional beat: survival versus the child's life, the book's central question made literal.

chapters.title: Through the Marsh
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The crossing: fever, leeches, a night of holding the baby above black water. Emotional beat: exhaustion stripped down to raw devotion—Marta calls the child by a name no one gave her.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Last Uniform
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The final barrier, manned by a boy soldier older-seeming than his years, who must decide whether orders or pity govern him. Emotional beat: Felix sees her younger self in him and cannot perform indifference anymore.

chapters.title: Ilves Closes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ilves corners them in a burned granary; Marta takes a bullet meant for Felix, and the cipher nearly burns with the roof. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh—someone else paid it.

chapters.title: What the Child Is Worth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, wounded and cornered. Ilves offers her old life back if she surrenders the documents and forgets the face, as instructed. Emotional beat: the temptation of invisibility offered one last time—and refused.

chapters.title: Forget Nothing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She turns the tables: the cipher names Ilves's own brothers among the sold garrisons. He lets her pass, undone. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon sharper than any seal she ever carried.

chapters.title: The Border Assembly
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She arrives at the rump parliament-in-exile as Corvane arrives to negotiate his amnesty. Emotional beat: two couriers of different truths meeting at the same door.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax, Felix's POV. Before the assembly, Felix breaks her deepest rule: she speaks, names herself, presents the cipher and the miniature. Corvane collapses; his faction scatters. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into voice—the invisible woman made witness.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Aftermath: Marta survives maimed; the republic's rebirth is messier than any dispatch promised; some conspirators walk free. Emotional beat: victory without vindication, honestly rendered.

chapters.title: A Name for the Child
chapters.summary: Felix and Marta's shared POV. They christen the girl Beatrix—'she who brings happiness'—and Felix formally gives up her courier's blank identity papers. Emotional beat: quiet joy after long cost.

chapters.title: Carried Forward
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Felix's POV, years later. Beatrix asks about the scarred satchel; Felix tells her the whole story, face remembered, nothing forgotten. Emotional beat: the letter finally delivered—not to a ministry, but to the next generation.
